source_text: ἔλεγον τεχθέντος αὐτοῦ· «δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις θεῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς εἰρήνη». 38 33.ν Περὶ προσκυνήσεως ἀνακεφαλαίωσις. 33.1 Εἴδομεν τοίνυν αὐτὸν δοξαζόμενον, εἴδομεν αὐτὸν καὶ προσκυνούμενον. 33.2 ἀμφότερα δὲ θεῷ ἐστιν πρέποντα καὶ ὀφειλόμενα, οὐχὶ δὲ κτίσματι, καθὰ γράφουσιν οἱ ὑποτεταγμένοι ἅγιοι· 33.3 ∆αυῒδ ἐν ϟδʹ ψαλμῷ· «δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν καὶ προσπέσωμεν αὐτῷ καὶ κλαύσωμεν ἐναντίον κυρίου τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἡμᾶς, ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν καὶ ἡμεῖς λαὸς νομῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ πρόβατα χειρὸς αὐτοῦ» 33.4 καὶ ἐν καʹ· «μνησθήσονται καὶ ἐπιστραφήσονται πρὸς κύριον πάντα τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ πᾶσαι αἱ πατριαὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν, ὅτι τοῦ κυρίου ἡ βασιλεία καὶ αὐτὸς δεσπόζει τῶν ἐθνῶν». 33.5 τί ἐροῦσιν ἄρα οἱ ἀπονέμοντες ὄνομα κεχωρισμένως τῷ μὲν πατρὶ τό «θεός», τῷ δὲ υἱῷ τό «κύριος», ἐπαΐοντες ἐνθάδε τὸν κύριον προσκυνεῖσθαι καὶ δεσπόζειν καὶ αὐτοῦ εἶναι τὴν βασιλείαν; 33.6 Καὶ πάλιν ἐν θʹ ψαλμῷ· «καὶ προσκυνήσω σε, κύριε, ἡ ἰσχύς μου»· 33.7 καὶ ἐν ρλαʹ· «προσκυνήσωμεν εἰς τὸν τόπον, οὗ ἔστησαν οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ»· 33.8 Παῦλος ἐκ τῆς ᾠδῆς τοῦ ∆ευτερονομίου γράφων· «ὅταν δὲ εἰσαγάγῃ τὸν πρωτότοκον εἰς τὴν οἰκουμένην, λέγει· καὶ προσκυ νησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι θεοῦ»· 33.9 καὶ ὁ εὐαγγελιστής «εἶπον», φησίν, «οἱ μάγοι· εἴδομεν αὐτοῦ τὸν ἀστέρα ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἤλθο μεν προσκυνῆσαι αὐτῷ»· 33.10 καὶ πάλιν «ἰδού», φησίν, «λεπρὸς ἦλθεν καὶ προσεκύνει αὐτῷ»· 33.11 καὶ πάλιν παρὰ Ματθαίῳ φησίν· «ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος. οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες· ἀλη θῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς εἶ», καὶ οὐ καθ' ἡμᾶς, φησίν, τοὺς ἀφθόνῳ δωρεᾷ ἐπικληθέντας υἱούς. 33.12 Καί· «ἄρχων τις προσεκύνει αὐτῷ». 33.13 καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ ὄρει φησίν· «οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἰδόντες αὐτὸν προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ». 34.ν Περὶ τῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν πατέρα πίστεως. 34.1 Καθὰ τοίνυν τῆς γραφῆς μείζονα ἢ περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς κατὰ τὸ φαινόμενον λεγούσης πολλὰ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ δηλούσης αὐτὸν παντοκράτορα, καὶ ποιητὴν τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ πάντων δημιουργόν, καὶ ἀληθινὸν θεόν, καὶ οὐκ ἔχοντα πρὸ αὐτοῦ θεόν, καὶ ἐπάνω πάντων, καὶ μέγαν καὶ ἐπὶ πάντων θεόν, πρὸς ὃν οὐ λογισθήσεται ἕτερος, καὶ ἐκ δεξιῶν συγκαθεζόμενον τῷ πατρί, καὶ εἰς τὸν κόλπον αὐτοῦ ὄντα, καὶ αὐτὸν εἶναι τὴν αἰώνιον ζωήν, καὶ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν, καὶ πάντων κύριον, καὶ μόνον δεσπότην, καὶ ἐξουσιαστήν, οὗτινος ἡ μὲν εἰρήνη οὐκ ἔχει ὅριον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπερέχει πάντα νοῦν, ἡ δὲ βασιλεία ἀτελεύτητος, καὶ ἐν μηδενὶ ἄλλῳ εἶναι τὴν σωτηρίαν, καὶ τὸν πατέρα ἕλκειν πρὸς τὸν υἱὸν τοὺς ἀξίους· κατ' οὐδὲν ὑποδεέστερος–μὴ γένοιτο– νομίζεται ὁ πατὴρ ἢ τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ. 34.2 Τὸν ἴσον τρόπον θεολογούσης περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς ὑψηλὰ οὐκ ὀφείλει ὡς μικρότερος ἢ ἀνόμοιος λογίζεσθαι ὁ μονογενὴς ἢ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα. 34.3 οὐδεμίας γὰρ κτιστῆς δυνάμεώς ἐστιν, μόνης δὲ τῆς ἀκτίστου τά τε μνημονευθέντα καὶ τὸ δημιουργεῖν οὐσίαν ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων, ἄλογόν τε καὶ λογικήν, 34.4 ζωοποιεῖν τε, ἁμαρτίας τε συγχωρεῖν, καὶ τὴν κτίσιν ἰδίαν λέγειν, καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἴσων γινώσκειν τὸν πατέρα, ὡς γινώσκεται ὑπ' αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἰσουργεῖν τῷ πατρί, καὶ εἶναι ἐν τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τὸν πατέρα ἐν αὐτῷ ἐξ ἴσου, ὑπὸ ἀγγέλων τε ὑπηρετεῖσθαι, καὶ τὸ ἔτι τούτων ὑπερτεροῦν τὸ μονογενῆ υἱὸν καὶ θεὸν καὶ φῶς ἐκ φωτὸς καὶ ζωὴν αἰώνιον καὶ ἀλήθειαν καὶ σωτῆρα μαρτυρεῖσθαι καὶ πανταχοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ πάντα ἐν αὐτῷ ἐστηρίχθαι, βασιλείαν τε οὐρανῶν καὶ τὴν θεϊκὴν εἰρήνην ὡς αὐτοῦ τυγχάνουσαν ἀβασκάνως πᾶσιν δωρεῖσθαι καὶ τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐπικαλουμένοις αὐτὸν τὴν ἐπὶ τῇ διηνεκεῖ σωτηρίᾳ παρέχειν ἀσφάλειαν. 34.5 Οἱ γὰρ κτίσμα καὶ οὐκ ἄναρχον καλοῦντες τὸν ἀληθινὸν υἱὸν θεοῦ καὶ τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ζωοποιὸν πνεῦμα οὐ 39 πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὰς ὑποστάσεις ταύτας, κἂν λέγωσι πιστεύειν· τάχα δὲ οὐδὲ εἰς τὸν πατέρα. 34.6 παραβαίνουσι γὰρ τὴν ἐντολὴν μὲν τοῦ παραγγέλλοντος πατρός· «ἄκουσον, λαός μου, καὶ λαλήσω σοι, Ἰσραήλ, καὶ διαμαρτυροῦμαι σοι, ἐὰν ἀκούσῃς μου· οὐκ ἔσται ἐν σοὶ θεὸς πρόσφατος οὐδὲ προσκυνήσεις θεῷ ἀλ λοτρίῳ» ἀντὶ τοῦ· οὐκ ὄντι ποτὲ ἢ ἑτεροουσίῳ· 34.7 καὶ «κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις» 34.8 καί «οὐκ ἔσονταί σοι θεοὶ ἕτεροι πλὴν ἐμοῦ» 34.9 καί «ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς, ὃς ἔχει τὴν ἐλπίδα ἐπ' ἄνθρωπον», τουτέστιν ἐπὶ ποίημα. 34.10 Τοῦτο δὲ τοῦ λέγοντος υἱοῦ ἐν Ματθαίῳ μέν· «οὐδεὶς δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν», τουτέστιν δύο φύσεσιν ἢ δεσποτείαις· ἐν Παύλῳ δὲ Ῥωμαίοις
pass_a_gloss: [...] they were saying, him having been born: 'glory in the highest to God and on earth peace'. 33.ν [Chapter title:] Summing up about worship. 33.1 We saw then him being glorified, we saw him also being worshipped. 33.2 And both are befitting and owed to God, and not to a creature, as the saints set out below write: 33.3 David in the 94th psalm (LXX; English 95): 'come, let us worship and fall before him and weep before the Lord who made us, because he is our God and we a people of his pasture and sheep of his hand'; 33.4 and in the 21st (English 22): 'all the ends of the earth will remember and turn back to the Lord, and all the families of the nations will worship before him, because the kingdom is the Lord's and he himself is master of the nations'. 33.5 What then will they say who assign a name separately, to the Father 'God' and to the Son 'Lord', hearing here that the Lord is worshipped and is master and that the kingdom is his? 33.6 And again in the 9th psalm: 'and I will worship you, Lord, my strength'; 33.7 and in the 131st (English 132): 'let us worship toward the place where his feet stood'; 33.8 Paul writing from the ode of Deuteronomy: 'and whenever he leads in the firstborn into the inhabited world, he says: and let all angels of God worship him'; 33.9 and the gospel-writer: 'the magi said', he says, 'we saw his star in the rising and came to worship him'; 33.10 and again: 'look', he says, 'a leper came and was worshipping him'; 33.11 and again in Matthew he says: 'the wind grew weary. And those in the boat worshipped him saying: truly you are a son of God', and not according to us, he says, who were called sons by an unbegrudged gift. 33.12 And: 'some ruler was worshipping him'. 33.13 And after his rising on the mountain he says: 'the apostles seeing him worshipped him'. 34.ν [Chapter title:] About faith toward God the Father. 34.1 Just as then, the writing saying many things about the Son greater than about the Father by the appearance, and making him plain as all-ruler, and maker of the ages, and craftsman of all things, and true God, and not having a God before him, and on top of all, and great and over-all God, toward whom another will not be reckoned, and sitting together at the right with the Father, and being into his bosom, and that he himself is the eternal life, and light the true one, and Lord of all, and only master, and holder of authority, of whom the peace has no boundary but even rises above every mind, and the kingdom is unending, and that the salvation is in no other, and that the Father drags toward the Son the worthy ones: in nothing is the Father thought lower, may it not happen, or his Spirit. 34.2 In the equal manner, it speaking of God about the Father high things, the only-begotten or the Holy Spirit is not owed to be counted as smaller or unlike. 34.3 For of no created power, but of the uncreated alone, are both the things recalled and to craft being out of things not being, unreasoning and reasoning, 34.4 and to make alive, and to let go sins, and to call the creation his own, and to know the Father out of equal terms as he is known by him, and to work equally with the Father, and to be in the Father and the Father in him on equal footing, and to be served by angels, and the thing still overtopping these, to be witnessed as only-begotten Son and God and light out of light and life eternal and truth and saviour, and to be present everywhere and all things to have been made firm in him, and to bestow without envy on all the kingdom of heavens and the godly peace as happening to be his, and to furnish to the believers calling on him the safety for the unbroken salvation. 34.5 For those calling a creature and not beginningless the true Son of God and the holy and life-making Spirit do not believe into these hypostases, even if they say they believe; and perhaps not even into the Father. 34.6 For they step past the command, on the one hand, of the charging Father: 'hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I bear witness to you, if you hear me: there will not be in you a fresh god, nor will you worship a foreign god', in place of: one not being at some time, or of another being; 34.7 and 'the Lord your God you will worship and him alone you will serve' 34.8 and 'there will not be for you other gods except me' 34.9 and 'accursed everyone who has the hope upon a human being', that is, upon a thing made. 34.10 And, on the other hand, this of the Son saying in Matthew: 'no one is able to be slave to two lords', that is, two natures or masterships; and in Paul to Romans [...]
pass_b_english: … were saying at his birth: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace” (Luke 2:14).

So we have seen him glorified, and we have seen him worshipped too. Both are fitting for God and owed to him, and not to a creature, as the saints cited below write. David, in the ninety-fifth Psalm: “Come, let us worship and fall down before him, and let us weep before the Lord who made us; for he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand” (Psalm 95:6-7). And in the twenty-second: “All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the Lord, and all the families of the nations shall worship before him; for the kingdom is the Lord’s, and he rules over the nations” (Psalm 22:27-28). What then will they say, who share out the names separately, “God” to the Father and “Lord” to the Son, when they hear here that the Lord is worshipped, that he rules, and that the kingdom is his?

And again, in the ninth Psalm: “And I will worship you, Lord, my strength.” And in the hundred and thirty-second: “Let us worship at the place where his feet stood” (Psalm 132:7). Paul, writing from the Song of Deuteronomy: “And when he brings the Firstborn into the world, he says: And let all the angels of God worship him” (Hebrews 1:6). And the evangelist: “The magi said,” he writes, “We saw his star in the east and have come to worship him” (Matthew 2:2). And again: “Behold,” he says, “a leper came and worshipped him” (Matthew 8:2). And again in Matthew he says: “The wind ceased. And those in the boat worshipped him, saying, Truly you are the Son of God” (Matthew 14:32-33); not, he means, in the way we are sons, who have been called so by a bountiful gift. And: “A certain ruler worshipped him” (Matthew 9:18). And after his resurrection, on the mountain, he says: “The apostles, when they saw him, worshipped him” (Matthew 28:16-17).
On faith in God the Father.

Scripture, then, says many things about the Son that are, to all appearance, greater than what it says about the Father. It declares him Almighty (Revelation 1:8), Maker of the ages (Hebrews 1:2), Creator of all things (John 1:3), true God (1 John 5:20), one who has no God before him (Isaiah 43:10), above all (John 3:31), the great God, God over all (Titus 2:13; Romans 9:5), to whom no other shall be compared (Baruch 3:35), seated with the Father at his right hand (Hebrews 1:3), and dwelling in his bosom (John 1:18). It says that he is eternal life and the true light (1 John 5:20; John 1:9), Lord of all (Acts 10:36), the only Master (Jude 4) and Sovereign, whose peace has no bound but surpasses all understanding (Philippians 4:7), and whose kingdom has no end (Luke 1:33); that salvation is in no one else (Acts 4:12); and that the Father draws the worthy to the Son (John 6:44). Yet the Father is not on that account thought in any respect inferior (God forbid!), nor is his Spirit.

In the same way, when Scripture speaks of the Father in lofty terms, the Only-begotten or the Holy Spirit ought not to be reckoned lesser or unlike. For none of the things just mentioned belongs to any created power, but to the uncreated alone: to create substance, both irrational and rational, out of what is not; to give life; to forgive sins (Mark 2:10); to call creation his own; to know the Father on equal terms, as he is known by him (John 10:15); to work as the Father works (John 5:19); to be in the Father and to have the Father in himself equally (John 14:10); and to be served by angels (Matthew 4:11). And, what surpasses even these, to be attested as only-begotten Son and God, light from light, eternal life, truth and Saviour; to be present everywhere; to have all things established in him; to give the kingdom of heaven and the divine peace, which is his own, ungrudgingly to all (John 14:27); and to grant believers who call on him a sure hold on everlasting salvation.

For those who call the true Son of God and the holy and life-giving Spirit a creature, and not without beginning, do not believe in these hypostases, even if they say they do; and perhaps they do not believe in the Father either. For they transgress the commandment of the Father, who charges: “Hear, my people, and I will speak to you; Israel, I will testify to you, if you will hear me: there shall be no new god among you, nor shall you worship a foreign god” (Psalm 50:7; Psalm 81:8-9), meaning one that once was not, or one of another substance. They transgress “You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve” (Deuteronomy 6:13; Matthew 4:10), and “You shall have no other gods besides me” (Exodus 20:3), and “Cursed is everyone who sets his hope on man” (Jeremiah 17:5), that is, on a thing made.
And they transgress this commandment of the Son as well, who says in Matthew: “No one can serve two lords” (Matthew 6:24), that is, two natures or two lordships; and in Paul, to the Romans …

choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English split 34.1 mid-sentence with '...' and lost its main clause (the Father is not thought inferior), wrote 'One who theologizes' for the genitive absolute of Scripture in 34.2, and misread ὑποτεταγμένοι ('the submissive saints'; it means the saints cited below), ἄναρχον ('not without a ruler'), ποίημα ('a work of art') and ἀφθόνῳ δωρεᾷ ('a cheap gift'). Wrong references fixed: 'Deuteronomy 6:4, 14' for the Father's charge (it is Psalm 50:7 run into Psalm 81:8-9); 'Psalm 72' for Greek Psalm 21 (Psalm 22:27-28); 'Psalm 29' for Didymus' 'ninth' Psalm (no inline reference now, see added_allusions). Bracket fillers [it says], [the true one], [the truth that] removed. Luke 2:14, Psalm 132:7, Hebrews 1:6, the Matthew worship texts and the Scripture titles of 34.1 and 34.4 now carry checked references. The chapter titles 33.ν and 34.ν stand as their own paragraphs.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence; its subject ('angels too') ends the previous section. Only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
Printed page numbers in the copy-text; page debris, not text.

choices.english: ninety-fifth, twenty-second, ninth, hundred and thirty-second Psalm
choices.why: Greek Psalm numbers converted to English (LXX 94 = 95, 21 = 22, 131 = 132). The 'ninth' is kept as Didymus gives it, since the words quoted match Greek Psalm 17:2 (English 18:1) with 'worship' for 'love'; see problems.
ὑποτάσσω here means 'set out below' (the list of witnesses that follows), not 'submissive'.

choices.english: not, he means, in the way we are sons
choices.why: φησίν marks Didymus' reading of the text; the contrast is between the Son by nature and sons by grace.

choices.term: κατ' οὐδὲν ὑποδεέστερος–μὴ γένοιτο– νομίζεται ὁ πατὴρ ἢ τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ
choices.english: Yet the Father is not on that account thought in any respect inferior (God forbid!), nor is his Spirit
choices.why: Main clause of the long period of 34.1; the parenthesis 'may it not be' recoils from the very thought and is kept in place.

choices.term: θεὸς πρόσφατος … θεῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ … ἀντὶ τοῦ· οὐκ ὄντι ποτὲ ἢ ἑτεροουσίῳ
choices.english: a new god … a foreign god … meaning one that once was not, or one of another substance
choices.why: Didymus glosses πρόσφατος as 'once not existing' and ἀλλότριος as 'of another substance', so 'new' and 'foreign' are kept literal for his argument to work.

choices.english: And they transgress this commandment of the Son as well
choices.why: The δέ answers the μέν of 34.6 ('the commandment of the Father'); the verb 'transgress' is carried over from there, not added.
